title: chivalry: medieval warfare
text: Even if I only spent about 100 hours with this game, I still have lots to say and many great memories to share about it. Chivalry Medieval Warfare is a first person, hack and slash medieval game, the combat is close and personal, each team, being able to choose from 4 classes: archer, man at arms, vanguard and knight. Each class has its speed and armour stats, and of course, specific weapons. There are 3 types of atacks: slashes, overhead and stab, the player being able to cancel them mid-swing in order to fool the enemy into blocking early. It's a great game, all in all, if you get it at a sale, but after rank 15 things start to fall apart, I met a lot of exploiters and hackers, if you just want to have some great time with your friends try staying under rank 15. I definitely recommend this game for the ones loving the middle ages and for the hack and slash fans, buy it.

text: Cities XL is a cheap cash in on the city builder genre. It does not inspire you, it isn't imaginative, and the game has bad controls overall. Comparing it to other city builders like sim city and cities skylines, it definitly lacks in many aspects. First the graphics, the two I previously mentioned are made by a big company and this is relativly indie. But, even on a indie budget the graphics look dull and dark there is no color to the game. Secondly, there isn't much to do in this game it's wrinse and repeat the whole way through. There is a 2:2:1 ratio for housing, commercial, and industrial, and if you keep this ratio throughout the game you can't fail. There aren't any challenging enviromental factors to deal with. Yes, you have to have oil, fertile land, and water, but if you don't have any of these resources you just click a button and you buy them. Lastly, the controls are complete garbage, It changes the regular controls for a city builder and puts them on random keys. So, you and build a city while stuck in an akward position you dont know how to change and at the end of the game finally find the key and you think to your self why would the developers put it there? text: A quite simple game for a clicker: click to deal damage, earn coins by killing mosters, use coins to upgrade heroes and soldiers you hire - no hard-core curency or economy or skill trees, etc. This game is fun and for a person with an interest in clickers would suit great. The one bad part of this game, or any clicker out there, is the grind. In order to beata hard boss, you will just go back to a few levels behind, and then sit there for 30-40 minutes, trying to raise the DPS and overall damage of your charachters. This cycle will repeat around every 5 levels (10 minutes of game time). If you are willing to aim for achievements, you are gone. Good, game. Clicker buff? Otherwise pass

title: clicker heroes
text: Decent game. Very slow to start, to the point where it takes a day or so to get your first ascention, best to first ascension at around 6-8 hero souls. Rinse and repeat till you get around 30 hero souls and try to get either Siyalatas for the idle build or Juggernaut for the active build, my personal recommendation is go for the active build. After you get juggernaut, get an auto clicker and game goes to easy mode. For an auto clicker, i recommend freemouseautoclicker from cnet(should be first link in google) since it can go upwards of 100 clicks per second and before people say that an autoclicker is cheating, it's actually supported on the game wiki. After a few days work, i was able to get to around floor 600-650 and get about 16 different ancients, 8 of which were maxed and i was getting around 3000 ish hero souls in a few hours. Very time consuming but the longer you play it, the easier to gets but at the same time, you get more absorbed by the game to the point where you start to think that 3000 hero souls gained in a few hours is too little. So you strive to get more and more and more. Great time waster though, played it nearly as much as i have played gmod.
